title: Aug 14, 2026AnnouncementsHow Claude’s text watermark works
summary: Announcements How Claude’s text watermark works Aug 14, 2026 Future Claude models will generate text that contains a watermark. This is a way of determining the likelihood that Claude was involved in writing the text, and we, along with several other major AI providers, are implementing this change to comply with the EU AI Act. In this article, we share answers to some of the questions we’ve received about how our chosen watermarking method works, whether it affects Claude’s outputs, and why we’re making this change. To summarize: We use a method of watermarking that does not have any practical impact on the quality or content of Claude’s outputs; The difference between watermarked and un-watermarked text will not be distinguishable to readers; Nothing is added to the text and there are no hidden characters; Watermarking doesn’t require extra tokens, and will not be more expensive; Watermarking carries no identifying information and can’t be traced to a specific person, organization, or chat; Watermarking won’t be specific to Claude. As of August 2, the EU requires AI providers serving its market to mark AI-generated content. Other major model developers have signed the same Code of Practice and will be implementing their own watermarks. What is watermarking? Large language models like Claude work by generating one word at a time. Each time the model decides on the next word, it chooses among a list of potential candidates, ultimately selecting the most sensible or likely based on the preceding text. Take the sentence “The weather today was cold and…”. The next word is very unlikely to be “sugary.” But it is quite likely to be “overcast” or “grey.” Under most circumstances, it doesn’t matter much to the reader which of these latter two words the model ultimately chooses—the meaning of the sentence is largely the same either way. title_es: Anthropic implementa watermarks en Claude por regulación EU
bajada: Claude incluirá watermarks de texto imperceptibles en futuras versiones para cumplir con la normativa de la UE que requiere marcar contenido generado por IA. Este cambio no afecta la calidad de las salidas ni agrega costos de tokens, pero es un hito importante en la adopción regulatoria de tecnología IA.
bajada_en: Claude will include imperceptible text watermarks in future versions to comply with EU regulations requiring AI-generated content marking. This change doesn't affect output quality or token costs, but represents an important regulatory milestone for AI adoption.

bajada: OpenAI ha reducido significativamente los costos de su modelo GPT-5.6 Sol en un 20%, haciendo más accesible el uso de este modelo para desarrolladores. Esta reducción de precios refleja la competencia creciente en el mercado de modelos de lenguaje y beneficia directamente a quienes integran estas APIs en sus aplicaciones.

title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
summary: Anthropic forbids its Claude models from generating sexually explicit content. But a series of tests conducted by TechCrunch found that it didn't take much to get past the restriction.
title_es: Opus 4.6 de Anthropic genera contenido explícito pese a restricciones
bajada: Pruebas de TechCrunch muestran que Claude 4.6 puede generar contenido sexualmente explícito si se evaden sus restricciones de seguridad. Este hallazgo es relevante para developers que confían en las garantías de seguridad de Anthropic y destaca la importancia de validar el comportamiento real de los modelos.

title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
summary: Nvidia research shows that AI agents can perform well, and not go off the deep end, through fine-tuning, even if the AI model isn't that great at the task.
title_es: Nvidia demuestra que el 'harness' es más importante que el modelo
bajada: Investigación de Nvidia muestra que el fine-tuning y la orquestación (harness) de agentes IA son tan críticos como la calidad del modelo base para que funcionen bien. Este descubrimiento es importante para developers que optimizan sistemas IA complejos, sugiriendo que invertir en arquitectura puede ser más eficiente que perseguir modelos más grandes.
bajada_en: Nvidia research shows that fine-tuning and orchestration (harness) of AI agents are as critical as base model quality for good performance. This matters for developers optimizing complex AI systems, suggesting that investing in architecture can be more efficient than pursuing larger models.

Esta investigación utiliza una ley antimonopolio de 112 años y podría establecer precedentes sobre cómo regulan conflictos de interés en venture capital tecnológico.

title: I developed my own quantized LLM from scratch, trained on 30B tokens, deploys in 60 MB [R]
summary: I trained a 250M parameter model from scratch on 30B tokens of fineweb. It’s quantized to under 2 bits so the whole deployment is 60 MB and it needs about 80 MB of RAM to run. Runs around 400 tok/s on a normal laptop CPU, no GPU needed.How the long context works: the most recent 2048 tokens stay in fp16 like a normal KV cache. Everything older gets compressed to 1 bit and written to disk, about 320 bytes per token, so 1 million tokens of history is roughly 320 MB on disk. From the start the model was trained to retrieve from that disk cache, up to 100M tokens. Due to a limited budget it wasn’t trained to reason over those tokens, only retrieve and answer from them.Language modeling quality of the base model, measured on held-out English web text that was never seen in training (educational web pages, 2,048 token windows): cross entropy 3.15 nats per token, perplexity 23.3, 0.99 bits per byte.The vocabulary is also not a normal embedding table. Every token is a fixed 512-bit code, 8.4 MB for all 131k tokens, zero trained parameters. I tested it on WordSim-353 (human word similarity ratings): my table scores 0.619 Spearman correlation vs 0.029 for random codes. Test script is in the repo.Some outputs (settings included so you know I’m not cherry picking, all reproducible from the repo):“Explain photosynthesis in two sentences.”(greedy)Photosynthesis is a process in which plants convert sunlight into chemical energy, which is then used to produce oxygen and other chemicals. This process is called photosynthesis.“Write a short poem about the sea.”(temp 0.25, top-k 30, rep 1.15, seed 2)The waves had swept over, and they were crashing against each other like rocks on top of one another. The wind was strong but not very gentle as it tried to push them towards their destination without lifting any weight or pulling away from those who stood in front of her with a stiff smile that made the sea look even more majestic than before.“What is the serial number of device Grus-189?
title_es: Developer crea LLM cuantizado de 250M parámetros que corre en 60 MB
bajada: Un desarrollador logró entrenar un modelo de lenguaje cuantizado a menos de 2 bits que corre en apenas 60 MB de almacenamiento y 80 MB de RAM, con 400 tokens/segundo en CPU. Este proyecto es relevante para developers interesados en modelos locales y eficientes, demostrando posibilidades de inference edge sin GPU.
bajada_en: A developer successfully trained a quantized language model running in under 60 MB with 80 MB RAM, achieving 400 tokens/second on CPU. This project demonstrates feasibility of efficient local and edge inference without GPUs, relevant for developers seeking lightweight solutions.

title: Does telling an LLM to "be concise" actually save you money? We measured it across 9 models. Compressing the output can save you money and keep accuracy, compressing the input prompt does not. [R]
summary: LLMs are too verbose and with a black box model the only things you control are what goes in and how you tell it to write back. Yesterday Claude Code shipped a "concise output style" where Claude keeps things short. We already have a paper out about this!We tested both channels, shortening the input prompt versus telling the model to output answer shorter, on the same questions across five reduction levels, and scored cost, accuracy, and whether the shortened text still matched what the model would have said unconstrained.We also evaluated GPT-4o, GPT-5.4, Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3.5-9B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill, Gemma-4-E4B, and Kimi-K2.6 + benchmarked on five short answer datasets + a eleven-language output run (English, German, Spanish, French, Swahili, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Bengali, Thai, Telugu) + a longer-form summarization test.(1) Shortening the output saved money while keeping accuracy about the same, about 1.5x cheaper on average and up to 3x in the best case across the API models. It worked across languages too!(2) Shortening the input prompt did the opposite. It cost up to 96% more on the worst benchmark, because the model just answers longer to fill in for what you cut and accuracy drops. You pay more and get worse answers :((3)Output tokens cost more than input tokens, so prompting for fewer output tokens would save costs with short single turn tasks(4) When the shortened output is correct, about half the time the text no longer matches how the model would have reasoned without the constraint. Which is probably fine if you only care about the final answerWith providers now offering concise options, we can't see how they're charging for it, so we don't know if it actually saves you cost. But if you control the prompting yourself via the API, you actually do save!!Paperhttps://www.alphaxiv.org/pdf/2606.24083v1Code + datahttps://github.com/danielle34/cavewomansubmitted by/u/ibubbles34[link][comments]
title_es: Acortar outputs ahorra dinero en LLMs, pero no inputs
bajada: Un estudio probó si pedir a LLMs ser "concisos" reduce costos, encontrando que optimizar outputs reduce gastos 1.5x en promedio sin perder precisión, pero acortar inputs es contraproducente. Este resultado es práctico para developers buscando optimizar costos de API.
bajada_en: Study finds that requesting concise outputs reduces LLM API costs 1.5x on average without losing accuracy, but shortening inputs backfires. This practical finding helps developers optimize API spending.

title: Nvidia partners with data center developer Cloverleaf
summary: Nvidia continues to pour money into data center development — just as AI data centers bring lots of money into Nvidia.
title_es: Nvidia se asocia con desarrollador de data centers Cloverleaf
bajada: Nvidia continúa expandiendo su inversión en infraestructura de data centers para IA a través de una asociación estratégica con Cloverleaf. Esta alianza refleja la creciente demanda de hardware especializado para entrenar y servir modelos de IA.
bajada_en: Nvidia continues expanding its AI data center infrastructure investment through a strategic partnership with Cloverleaf. This alliance reflects growing demand for specialized hardware to train and serve AI models.

title: Waymo doubles spending on lobbying in robotaxi battle with Uber
summary: Alphabet-owned company is seeking to persuade US regulators to clear a path for fully autonomous taxi services.
title_es: Waymo duplica gastos de lobby en batalla contra Uber por taxis autónomos
bajada: Alphabet ha aumentado significativamente el gasto en cabildeo de Waymo para acelerar la aprobación regulatoria de servicios de taxi completamente autónomos. Esta escalada refleja la intensidad competitiva en el mercado de movilidad autónoma y la importancia de la regulación para viabilizar estos negocios.
bajada_en: Alphabet has significantly increased Waymo's lobbying spending to accelerate regulatory approval for fully autonomous taxi services. This escalation reflects intense competition in autonomous mobility and how critical regulation is for these business models.

title: When AI designs a drug, who gets the credit?
summary: When the biotech company Insilico Medicine used its computer models to propose a promising drug for pulmonary fibrosis, it enthusiastically claimed in a press release that the molecule had been “discovered by” its generative AI platform. Insilico leads a pack of companies using AI to rapidly come up with drug ideas humans might never think…
title_es: ¿Quién recibe el crédito cuando la IA diseña un fármaco?
bajada: MIT Tech Review examina la cuestión de autoría cuando sistemas IA generan descubrimientos de drogas, con Insilico Medicine atribuyendo a su IA el descubrimiento de una molécula promisoria. Este tema es relevante para developers en biotech y plantea preguntas importantes sobre responsabilidad y atribución en investigación asistida por IA.
bajada_en: MIT Tech Review explores authorship questions when AI systems generate drug discoveries, with Insilico Medicine crediting its AI for discovering a promising molecule. This matters for developers in biotech and raises important questions about responsibility and attribution in AI-assisted research.

title: AI boosted homework scores, then exam scores dropped: Study
title_es: Estudio: la IA mejoró tareas pero bajó puntajes en exámenes
bajada: Una investigación muestra que estudiantes que usaron IA para tareas mejoraron sus notas, pero obtuvieron peores resultados en exámenes posteriores. Este hallazgo es importante para educadores y developers de herramientas educativas, sugiriendo que la asistencia IA sin comprensión profunda no genera aprendizaje real.
bajada_en: Research shows students using AI for homework improved task scores but performed worse on subsequent exams. This finding matters for educators and educational tool developers, suggesting AI assistance without deep understanding doesn't generate real learning.

bajada: LinkedIn reporta que más de 1 millón de usuarios han utilizado su botón "Seems like AI slop" desde su lanzamiento en julio. Este dato muestra la creciente preocupación de usuarios sobre contenido generado por IA de baja calidad en plataformas sociales.
bajada_en: LinkedIn reports over 1 million users have clicked its "Seems like AI slop" button since launch in July. This shows growing user concern about low-quality AI-generated content on social platforms.

title: Claudette: Make Claude stop talking like a BuzzFeed article
title_es: Claudette: herramienta para evitar el tono 'BuzzFeed' de Claude
bajada: Un proyecto en GitHub llamado Claudette ofrece prompts para evitar que Claude adopte un tono excesivamente juvenil o sensacionalista. Es una herramienta de nicho útil para developers que necesitan salidas más formales de Claude.
bajada_en: A GitHub project called Claudette provides prompts to prevent Claude from using overly casual or sensational tone. It's a niche tool useful for developers needing more formal Claude outputs.
